english.html: is no new thing that two persons should resemble each other, not only in the features and lineaments of the face, but also in certain particular signs of the body.

That it is so: Sura, a Roman, being proconsul in Sicily, found there a poor fisherman altogether like him, not only in the bulk and stature of the body, in the features of the mouth and the lineaments of the face, but also in his gestures and bearing, and in I know not what opening of the mouth which the said Sura had, proper and particular to himself, in laughing or in speaking — nay, even in being a stammerer, like him <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>. So it was with the father of the great Pompey and his cook, as we shall say hereafter <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>.

notes.citation: Pliny, Natural History VII.10 (§55, the Sicilian fisherman who resembled the proconsul Sura even to the stammer; the chapter is c. 12 in the old division, so the printed c. xxiij is probably a slip); Valerius Maximus, Memorable Doings and Sayings IX.14 (De similitudine formae; Coras's c. 15 in the old numbering, printed vx for xv)
notes.original: Pline au li. vij. c. xxiij. Va lere au liu. ix. c. vx.
notes.gloss: Pliny: the resemblance extended to the gaping of the mouth and the hesitation of the tongue; Valerius tells the retort about Sura's father (cf. annot-005 {f}).

notes.citation: Coras's own Annotation LXIII, as printed; the matter of Pompey's father and his cook Menogenes is in fact told in Annotation LXII (p084)
notes.gloss: The cross-reference is off by one; the story is in the annotation numbered LXII in this edition.

english.html: And as to saying that by the inquiries it is reported that the rumour at the said place of Artigat is that Pierre Guerre and his sons-in-law were constraining the said de Rols to carry on the prosecution: it is answered that proof by rumour and common repute is not received, save in certain cases which could not be made to fit here.
